name: Hooded Pullover (Bleach-Stained, Restitched Hood)
description: A mid-weight pullover hoodie in what was once charcoal grey, now streaked with pale bleach blotches across the left shoulder and hem. The hood drawstring is a replacement — a length of thin paracord knotted through the original eyelets. Kangaroo pocket seam has been restitched in a visible white running stitch.
functionality: Hood provides wind and light rain protection; kangaroo pocket holds small essentials with hands-free carry.
what_it_says: Worn-in and repaired — this person holds onto things, doesn't let go easily.
story_hooks: The bleach pattern on the shoulder looks almost deliberate — some people on the Shelf bleach-tag their own clothes as a low-key identifier.
The paracord drawstring is long enough to be useful for other things; whoever replaced it knew exactly what they were doing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A worn, heavily modified hoodie that reads as street-salvage with utilitarian repairs. The silhouette is relaxed and slightly oversized, slouching at the shoulders. Bleach damage creates an accidental, asymmetrical tie-dye effect that gives it character despite (or because of) its deterioration.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and oversized through the body and arms, with a dropped shoulder seam. Hood sits generously over the head without compression. Kangaroo pocket hangs slightly loose due to age.
physical_description.primary_material: Mid-weight cotton-synthetic blend, likely salvaged or mass-produced pre-2210. Fabric has softened from repeated washing and wear.
physical_description.texture: Soft, broken-in surface with slight pilling at stress points. Bleach damage creates matte white streaks against the dull grey. Restitched seams are slightly raised and more rigid than surrounding fabric.
physical_description.color_scheme: Base charcoal grey faded to a murky slate. Irregular pale bleach blotches concentrated on left shoulder and lower hem. Stark white paracord drawstring and visible white running stitch on pocket create high-contrast repair details.
physical_description.closures: Traditional drawstring hood using thin paracord (replacement) threaded through original metal eyelets. No front zipper — pure pullover. Kangaroo pocket is open.
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical bleach staining (accidental or intentional weathering)
Paracord replacement drawstring — clearly knotted, not factory
Visible white running stitch on kangaroo pocket seam (hand-repaired)
Original metal eyelets surviving despite garment age
No visible manufacturer mark or branding
Slight fading and color variation suggesting multiple wash cycles
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 — Working class salvage or sub-grade personal wear. No corporate finish, fully functional but clearly repaired.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by street-level workers, salvage runners, or undercity residents who value function over aesthetics. The visible repairs signal self-sufficiency and DIY culture. Could belong to someone operating in the ungoverned zones or living paycheck-to-paycheck in the GLMZ underbelly.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered and broken-in. Bleach damage is permanent and uneven. Repairs are visible and intentional. Would show additional wear with use — fraying drawstring, slight holes forming at seams, progressive fading.
